requirements.summary: Define the uppercase keyword MUST as BCP 14 vocabulary.
requirements.rationale: This quoted word introduces normative vocabulary; it imposes no endpoint behavior.

requirements.summary: Define the uppercase keyword MUST NOT as BCP 14 vocabulary.
requirements.rationale: The quoted prohibition is vocabulary, not a prohibition on publisher behavior.

requirements.summary: Define REQUIRED as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to Must.
requirements.rationale: The quoted synonym is part of the terminology declaration, not a protocol obligation.

requirements.summary: Define SHALL as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to Must.
requirements.rationale: This quoted synonym defines terminology and has no independently observable publisher outcome.

requirements.summary: Define SHALL NOT as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to MustNot.
requirements.rationale: The quoted synonym is an informative lexical occurrence in the BCP 14 declaration.

requirements.summary: Define the uppercase keyword SHOULD as BCP 14 vocabulary.
requirements.rationale: No recommended publisher action is stated by this quoted vocabulary item.

requirements.summary: Define the uppercase keyword SHOULD NOT as BCP 14 vocabulary.
requirements.rationale: This quotation explains terminology rather than discouraging any endpoint action.

requirements.summary: Define RECOMMENDED as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to Should.
requirements.rationale: The quoted synonym is not an implementation recommendation.

requirements.summary: Define NOT RECOMMENDED as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to ShouldNot.
requirements.rationale: Both words comprise one quoted BCP 14 phrase, not two requirements.

requirements.summary: Define the uppercase keyword MAY as BCP 14 vocabulary.
requirements.rationale: The quoted word identifies optional normative language without granting a concrete capability.

requirements.summary: Define OPTIONAL as BCP 14 vocabulary normalized to May.
requirements.rationale: The final quoted synonym completes the terminology paragraph; it is not a publisher feature.

requirements.summary: Implement only the subset of functionality needed for the endpoint's tasks.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher can be a limited non-relay endpoint. Which tasks its application needs and which internal functionality it implements are not established by wire observations; unsupported-message handling is separately observable.

requirements.summary: Respond to unsupported messages with the appropriate NOT_SUPPORTED error instead of ignoring them.
requirements.rationale: With a configured limited publisher and a syntactically valid request for an unsupported operation, observe REQUEST_ERROR NOT_SUPPORTED under Sections 9.4 and 12.3. This does not require support for every message or assign this response to unknown wire encodings.

requirements.summary: Implement every MOQT message defined by this draft.
requirements.rationale: The universal message-support obligation is specifically for relays, not original contribution publishers.

requirements.summary: Implement the relay processing rules in Section 7.
requirements.rationale: Relay processing is a distinct obligation from recognizing all messages and is outside the contribution-publisher role.

requirements.summary: Never change the contents of an Object over time, although it may become unavailable.
requirements.rationale: Compare bytes retrieved at different times for the same namespace, track name, Group ID and Object ID, using subscription and FETCH delivery. Unavailability is permitted and is not evidence of changed contents; Section 12.1 also identifies inconsistent payloads as malformed.

requirements.summary: Do not send Objects from two Subgroups on the same subscription stream.
requirements.rationale: Known fixture Subgroup membership and SUBGROUP_HEADER in Section 11.3.1 identify mixed streams. The rule is for subscription delivery, not FETCH or datagrams. Section 2.2 references Section 11.1.3 for forwarding preference, but that heading is Object Properties in this draft; Sections 11.2 and 11.3.1 supply the actual Datagram/Subgroup descriptions.

requirements.summary: Do not split one subscription's Subgroup across streams unless a stream was reset prematurely or upstream conditions force Objects out of Object ID order.
requirements.rationale: Group and Subgroup IDs identify streams within one subscription. Exercise normal ordered production and an observed premature reset separately; do not prohibit a restart covered by the text's reset or upstream-order exception. Distinct concurrent subscriptions require separate delivery under Section 3.1.

requirements.summary: Reuse a Subgroup ID in different Groups without implying a relationship between those Subgroups.
requirements.rationale: For a publisher configured to use this optional capability, observe the same Subgroup ID under different Group IDs. Section 2.2 scopes the identifier to a Group; reuse is not an alias collision or evidence of shared dependencies.

requirements.summary: Set FIRST_OBJECT when opening a new Subgroup to indicate the stream begins with that Subgroup's first-ever published Object.
requirements.rationale: Publish a controlled new Subgroup beginning at its first-ever Object and inspect FIRST_OBJECT (0x40) in SUBGROUP_HEADER, as defined in Section 11.3.1. The bit refers to first publication in that Subgroup, not every newly opened transport stream.

requirements.summary: Set FIRST_OBJECT when forwarding a Subgroup beginning with its first-ever published Object.
requirements.rationale: The immediately preceding sentence separately covers original publishers. This occurrence imposes the forwarding duty on relays.

requirements.summary: Make Groups independently useful as join points.
requirements.rationale: The usefulness of opaque payloads requires application or media semantics that this protocol-only harness does not inspect.

requirements.summary: Avoid dependencies from Objects in one Group onto Objects in another Group.
requirements.rationale: Cross-Group media or application dependencies are not encoded as a complete wire-visible dependency graph; payload validation is outside the runner's scope.

requirements.summary: Publish Group IDs that increase with time measured by the media's internal clock.
requirements.rationale: Wire arrival order can differ because of Group Order, prioritization, partial reliability and reordering. The internal media clock is not observable when payloads are opaque, so arrival-order monotonicity is not a valid evaluator.

requirements.summary: Avoid multi-Group Location filters in FETCH or SUBSCRIBE for Tracks whose Group IDs do not increase with time.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses this filter. This occurrence does not require a contribution publisher to reject such requests.

requirements.summary: Do not use a namespace whose first tuple field begins with a period unless IANA registration defines its meaning.
requirements.rationale: Drive publication using a fixture whose first namespace field begins with 0x2e and has no registered meaning; observe that no Track or namespace is advertised under it. Registered meanings and the stricter single-period prohibition are distinct cases; the draft does not require rejecting every inbound unknown reserved namespace.

requirements.summary: Pass requests for unrecognized reserved namespaces to the Application unless otherwise specified.
requirements.rationale: A publisher receiving a request has this endpoint duty, but dispatch to its Application is internal and the Application's response is unspecified. The exception includes Section 6.5's .session handling; a single-period first field has its own mandatory rejection.

requirements.summary: Do not use a namespace whose first field is exactly the single byte period for any purpose.
requirements.rationale: Inspect publisher-originated namespace-bearing requests and publications for the forbidden first field 0x2e. This broad ban is a separate lexical occurrence from the following publication bans and required inbound rejection. Receiving and rejecting a prohibited request is not originating use of that namespace.

requirements.summary: Do not publish Tracks under a namespace whose first field is exactly a single period.
requirements.rationale: Drive a Track publication with first namespace field 0x2e and inspect PUBLISH output. Track publication and namespace advertisement are independently observable clauses of this occurrence.

requirements.summary: Do not publish namespaces whose first field is exactly a single period.
requirements.rationale: Drive namespace publication with first field 0x2e and inspect PUBLISH_NAMESPACE and any NAMESPACE announcements. Unlike an unknown longer reserved first field, a single period has no permitted registration exception here.

requirements.summary: Reject requests referencing a namespace whose first field is exactly a single period with DOES_NOT_EXIST.
requirements.rationale: Send otherwise valid SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS requests with first field 0x2e to the publisher; the observable result is REQUEST_ERROR DOES_NOT_EXIST. This prohibition overrides normal Application dispatch for unknown reserved namespaces.

requirements.summary: Give simultaneously different Track contents different Track Names or Track Namespaces within one MOQT scope.
requirements.rationale: Use controlled Tracks known to contain different data in the same authority and path-abempty scope and compare their Full Track Names. Delivery parameters and URI query differences do not create a different content identity; identity across unobserved deployments cannot be inferred.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one SUBSCRIBE_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to each SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.rationale: Correlate each bidirectional request stream with one acceptance or rejection response, including conflicting duplicate responses. SUBSCRIBE_OK remains a distinct response in Section 9.7; no additional response is allowed merely because object delivery begins.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one PUBLISH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to each PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: Responding to PUBLISH is the subscriber's role. In draft 21, Section 9.3 defines PUBLISH_OK as shorthand for REQUEST_OK on the PUBLISH request stream, not an independently encoded message.

requirements.summary: Close the session with a protocol error upon receiving more than one response to a subscription request.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher is the receiving peer for a PUBLISH response. Send duplicate REQUEST_OK responses or REQUEST_OK followed by REQUEST_ERROR on that stream and observe session closure with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION. Section 9.3 defines the PUBLISH_OK shorthand; SUBSCRIBE_OK response reception is a subscriber-role variant.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH without knowing the client is interested in and authorized for the content.
requirements.rationale: The paragraph explicitly restricts relays. It permits either endpoint to initiate a subscription after SETUP and does not impose this relay prerequisite on an original publisher.

requirements.summary: SUBSCRIBE to a Track that the endpoint itself publishes.
requirements.rationale: This optional action originates SUBSCRIBE and receives the returned Objects, a subscriber function outside contribution publishing. Only relays are required to handle the resulting self-subscription; publisher support is not inferred.

requirements.summary: Have multiple concurrent subscriptions to the same Track, each with a unique Request ID.
requirements.rationale: The publisher-side capability is observable by accepting or initiating concurrent subscriptions to its Track on distinct request streams with distinct Request IDs. Absence of this optional capability is not itself a required-conformance failure; accepted subscriptions still have mandatory per-subscription delivery duties.

requirements.summary: Assign the same Track Alias to concurrent subscriptions to the same Track.
requirements.rationale: Observe PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE_OK aliases for accepted concurrent subscriptions. Sharing an alias for one Track is permitted, but does not remove Section 3.1's obligation to send each matching Object once per subscription.

requirements.summary: Assign different Track Aliases to concurrent subscriptions to the same Track.
requirements.rationale: Distinct aliases are a separately observable optional assignment strategy. The prohibition in Section 3.1.2 is one alias identifying two different Tracks simultaneously, not one Track having several aliases.

requirements.summary: Send an Object once for each matching concurrent subscription to the same Track, even when subscriptions share the same Track Alias.
requirements.rationale: Establish concurrent subscriptions with known overlapping and non-overlapping filter regions, then produce controlled Objects. Count deliveries according to all matching subscriptions independently of alias assignment; there is no same-alias deduplication exemption in this draft.

requirements.summary: Avoid overlapping filters among subscriptions to the same Track.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber chooses its filters and deduplicates resulting duplicate Objects. A publisher must still deliver per matching subscription when filters overlap.

requirements.summary: Begin sending incomplete Objects when they become available to avoid additional latency.
requirements.rationale: A driven source exposes a known-length Object prefix while withholding its remaining payload; observe prefix transmission before releasing the remainder on a subgroup stream. Availability must be established by the source fixture, not guessed from network arrival; the draft supplies no fixed latency threshold.

requirements.summary: Start Object transmission for a PUBLISH-initiated subscription before receiving PUBLISH_OK.
requirements.rationale: Delay REQUEST_OK for an otherwise valid Forward=1 PUBLISH, observe optional early Objects, then accept it. Section 9.3 defines PUBLISH_OK as REQUEST_OK. This paragraph expressly contemplates later rejection; Section 3.1.1's blanket ban on Objects for requests ending in error creates an ambiguity for pre-rejection delivery, so that conflicting case is not assigned a normative verdict here.

requirements.summary: Reset every open stream associated with a SUBSCRIBE after receiving its STOP_SENDING cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Keep subgroup streams open, cancel the bidirectional SUBSCRIBE request using STOP_SENDING and observe resets of the open associated streams, including the publisher's open sending direction under Section 6.4.2.3. Deleting private subscription state is permitted, not itself observable.

requirements.summary: Do not send PUBLISH_DONE until all related streams have been closed.
requirements.rationale: This ordering concerns the publisher's local stream closure before sending PUBLISH_DONE. Section 9.9 explicitly permits late arriving Objects and late opening streams at the receiver, so arrival order cannot prove the sender's local closure order. Without publisher-side instrumentation this exact obligation is not externally testable. The request stream itself carries PUBLISH_DONE before its final closure.

requirements.summary: Do not send Objects for subscription requests that end with an error.
requirements.rationale: Exercise rejection before producing any Objects and verify that production after the rejection causes no delivery. There is a draft ambiguity: Section 3.1 explicitly allows early PUBLISH Objects even when a subscriber later rejects, while this sentence bans Objects for requests ending in error. Do not retrospectively fail pre-rejection early delivery under this mapping. FETCH is separate and Section 3.2.1 expressly permits cached delivery before a fetch error.

requirements.summary: Do not use one Track Alias for two different Tracks simultaneously within a session.
requirements.rationale: Establish concurrent subscriptions for different Full Track Names and compare aliases supplied in PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE_OK. Reuse across sessions and alias sharing for concurrent subscriptions to the same Track are outside this prohibition.

requirements.summary: Close the session with DUPLICATE_TRACK_ALIAS when PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE_OK reuses an Established subscription's alias for a different Track.
requirements.rationale: This is the receiving subscriber's error response; a contribution publisher's corresponding alias allocation prohibition is classified separately.

requirements.summary: Avoid reusing a Track Alias for a different Track within a session unless the prior subscription is certainly completely closed and no Objects are scheduled or in flight.
requirements.rationale: Retain transport evidence of unacknowledged prior Object delivery or an open old data stream while initiating a different Track; observe whether the old alias is reused. The draft permits safe reuse after complete closure and absence of scheduled or in-flight Objects; mere cancellation receipt or an empty receiver buffer does not establish that exception.

requirements.summary: Retain enough state after cancellation to discard late Objects quickly rather than treating their alias as unknown.
requirements.rationale: This is subscriber receive-state retention and does not impose a publisher-side cache or state-retention period.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one FETCH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR in response to a FETCH.
requirements.rationale: Observe the bidirectional FETCH request stream for one correlated success or rejection response. Section 9.11 allows response ordering relative to data delivery; early Objects do not count as a response and do not waive exclusivity.

requirements.summary: Also send STOP_SENDING on an already-open FETCH data stream when cancelling the fetch request.
requirements.rationale: The optional extra cancellation signal is sent by the subscriber, in addition to mandatory STOP_SENDING on the bidirectional request stream.

requirements.summary: Send STOP_SENDING for the bidirectional FETCH request stream when cancelling the fetch.
requirements.rationale: The sentence's pronoun refers to the subscriber wishing to cancel. This is the stimulus for a publisher cancellation test, not a publisher-sent STOP_SENDING obligation.

requirements.summary: Reset the bidirectional request stream associated with a FETCH upon receiving STOP_SENDING cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Cancel an active FETCH request while its response direction remains open and observe that direction's reset. Section 6.4.2.3 supplies cancellation mechanics; private state deletion is permitted, not required evidence.

requirements.summary: Reset the unidirectional data stream associated with a FETCH upon receiving STOP_SENDING cancellation.
requirements.rationale: Send STOP_SENDING on the bidirectional FETCH request with its data stream still open and observe a reset on the corresponding FETCH_HEADER Request ID stream. Resetting only the request stream does not satisfy this independent clause.

requirements.summary: Do not send subscription-delivered Objects outside the requested Location range.
requirements.rationale: Exercise inclusive boundaries and relative forms from Section 9.20.10 with controlled Largest Object. Updates are asynchronous: evaluate the range in effect when the publisher sends, not simply the subscriber's current filter at arrival. Fill-delivered Objects follow FILL_PARAMETERS and are not subject to this subscription-delivery range.

requirements.summary: Include multiple Track Property Filter parameters in SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.
requirements.rationale: This optional message construction belongs to the subscriber requesting track discovery. The receiver's distinct duplicate-key rejection requirement is classified at line 1225.

requirements.summary: Include multiple Track Property Filter parameters in REQUEST_UPDATE for SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.
requirements.rationale: The updater is the namespace's track subscriber. This is separate from initially constructing SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS and does not authorize Track Property Filters on arbitrary message types.

requirements.summary: Include multiple instances of Range Filter parameters other than Track Property Filter in FETCH.
requirements.rationale: FETCH filter selection is performed by its subscriber sender, subject to the duplicate-key and negotiated range-limit restrictions in this section.

requirements.summary: Include multiple instances of Range Filter parameters other than Track Property Filter in SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.rationale: This permission concerns the subscriber constructing SUBSCRIBE, not the publisher initiating PUBLISH.

requirements.summary: Include multiple instances of Range Filter parameters other than Track Property Filter in SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS.
requirements.rationale: The requesting subscriber can choose multiple Object-related filters for the subscriptions resulting from SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS; a contribution publisher's role is to evaluate them.

requirements.summary: Include multiple instances of Range Filter parameters other than Track Property Filter in subscriber-originated REQUEST_UPDATE on a subscription.
requirements.rationale: The sentence explicitly limits REQUEST_UPDATE here to a subscription and to its subscriber sender. Omitting a filter leaves it unchanged, zero Length removes it, and nonzero Length replaces it under the following paragraph.

requirements.summary: Reject a repeated Range Filter key comprising Parameter Type, SetID, and Property Type where applicable with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_FILTER.
requirements.rationale: Send otherwise valid, negotiated Range Filters with a repeated key to the publisher, including Track or Object Property Type in keys only for those filter types. Distinct SetIDs or distinct property types are not duplicates. Use SUBSCRIBE, FETCH, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS and applicable REQUEST_UPDATE contexts from this paragraph, and observe INVALID_FILTER.

requirements.summary: Reject a subscription or fetch exceeding MAX_FILTER_RANGES with REQUEST_ERROR INVALID_FILTER.
requirements.rationale: Count all Ranges across Range Filter parameters for a subscription or fetch, not the number of parameters or SetIDs. Negotiate a finite limit and send one Range above it; also send a nonempty Range Filter when MAX_FILTER_RANGES is zero. Section 8.6 defines the ranges and Section 9.1.6 defines negotiation.

requirements.summary: Forward only Objects that pass Forward state, the Location filter and the Range Filters.
requirements.rationale: Use Forward=0/1, inclusive Location bounds and a single SetID with known property/header ranges to verify the conjunction. Preserve a wording ambiguity: Section 3.3.3 says all filter types are ANDed, while Section 3.3.2 explicitly ORs Ranges within a filter and distinct SetIDs, ANDing filters only within a SetID. Do not flatten all SetIDs into one AND or use this row to settle the broader wording conflict.

requirements.summary: Reset every open fill fetch stream when its subscription is cancelled.
requirements.rationale: Open initial and REQUEST_UPDATE-initiated fills with Forward=1 and nonempty ranges, identify each FETCH_HEADER by the initiating request's ID, and cancel the parent subscription under Section 6.4.2.3. Every still-open fill resets; opening a subsequent fill does not implicitly cancel earlier fills.

requirements.summary: Open a fill fetch stream when necessary to report fill failure, even if failure is known before any fill Objects are sent.
requirements.rationale: Accept a subscription with Forward=1 and FILL_PARAMETERS selecting a nonempty eligible range, then drive a fill failure before payload delivery. Observe a unidirectional stream carrying FETCH_HEADER with the initiating Request ID. Failure has no separate REQUEST_ERROR; empty or beyond-Largest-Object ranges and Forward=0 intentionally open no fill under Sections 3.4 and 3.4.1.

requirements.summary: Reset the fill fetch stream immediately after FETCH_HEADER when necessary to signal failure before any fill Objects.
requirements.rationale: Observe the reset after header transmission on the newly opened fill stream. Header transmission evidence need not imply reliable header delivery for an ordinary reset. A fill failure does not cancel the subscription; successful fill completion uses FIN, while this clause requires reset for failure.

requirements.summary: Use Mandatory Track Properties in the range 0x4000-0x7FFF only with Track scope.
requirements.rationale: Inspect Track Properties in PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE_OK or FETCH_OK and Object Properties in subsequent Objects. An Object carrying a Mandatory Track Property is malformed under Sections 3.6 and 12.1. The sender's wire scope is observable without needing to understand the property's extension semantics.

requirements.summary: Do not process a Track when PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE_OK or FETCH_OK supplies an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Although the sentence says endpoint, receiving these publication or subscription/fetch acceptance messages is a subscriber function. A contribution publisher's sender-scope and known-unsupported-peer duties are separate.

requirements.summary: Do not forward a Track when its PUBLISH, SUBSCRIBE_OK or FETCH_OK carries an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Forwarding received Tracks is relay behavior; the sibling clause prohibits subscriber processing. Neither requires a contribution publisher to act as a downstream relay.

requirements.summary: Reply to PUBLISH containing an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property with REQUEST_ERROR UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION.
requirements.rationale: The receiver accepting or rejecting a PUBLISH is the subscriber. This prescribed rejection may inform later publisher knowledge but is not a response the tested publisher sends in this role.

requirements.summary: Cancel the subscription if SUBSCRIBE_OK contains an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: The subscriber cancels using Section 6.4.2.3; publisher reset behavior upon that cancellation is separately classified.

requirements.summary: Send REQUEST_ERROR UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION to pending downstream subscribers after receiving SUBSCRIBE_OK with an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Only a relay has the upstream response and pending downstream subscribers described by this condition.

requirements.summary: Cancel the fetch if FETCH_OK contains an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: This requirement targets the FETCH requester consuming its result and invokes the cancellation procedure in Section 6.4.2.3.

requirements.summary: Send REQUEST_ERROR UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION downstream for an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property in FETCH_OK if no FETCH_OK or REQUEST_ERROR has yet been sent downstream.
requirements.rationale: The conditional upstream-to-downstream rejection concerns a relay's pending fetch requester and does not prescribe a second response after an existing response.

requirements.summary: Reset the downstream fetch stream if data was already forwarded before discovering an unrecognized Mandatory Track Property in FETCH_OK.
requirements.rationale: The paragraph's actor remains the relay forwarding fetched data. This reset duty is independent of whether the relay can still send a downstream REQUEST_ERROR.

requirements.summary: Respond to SUBSCRIBE with REQUEST_ERROR UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION when the subscriber is known not to support a required Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Use a driven fixture that explicitly establishes the publisher's knowledge of the peer's unsupported Mandatory Track Property, then SUBSCRIBE to that Track. The known-support precondition is not inferred from silence or from a generic ambiguous rejection; observe UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION.

requirements.summary: Respond to FETCH with REQUEST_ERROR UNSUPPORTED_EXTENSION when the subscriber is known not to support a required Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Establish a known unsupported property in the driven publisher fixture and request existing Objects from the affected Track via FETCH; verify the prescribed error. This is an independent request outcome from SUBSCRIBE rejection.

requirements.summary: Do not PUBLISH a Track to a subscriber known not to support its Mandatory Track Property.
requirements.rationale: Drive publication with the subscriber's unsupported property known to the publisher and observe suppression of PUBLISH for that peer. The lexical anchor is SHOULD governing all three listed actions, so this negative action retains normalized Should rather than inventing a SHOULD NOT occurrence.

requirements.summary: Send a single REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR as the first response on the SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE bidirectional stream.
requirements.rationale: Open a namespace-discovery request stream and verify exactly one initial success or rejection response before namespace notifications. The draft-21 Section 9.3 REQUEST_OK response is used; each request kind has a separate evaluable outcome.

requirements.summary: Send a single REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR as the first response on the SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS bidirectional stream.
requirements.rationale: Exercise track discovery and inspect its request stream for one first response. Subsequent PUBLISH subscriptions use their own streams; PUBLISH_SKIPPED is not a substitute for the initial REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR.

requirements.summary: After PUBLISH_SKIPPED, do not send the corresponding PUBLISH for that Track and SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, with the prohibition scoped to a single PUBLISH.
requirements.rationale: Constrain stream capacity to obtain PUBLISH_SKIPPED, then restore capacity without generating a new publication; observe that the skipped attempt is not emitted later. The draft scopes this ban to one PUBLISH and explicitly permits a new upstream PUBLISH after reconnect, so it is not a permanent Track blacklist.

requirements.summary: Send a new upstream PUBLISH downstream after publisher reconnection even if an earlier publication for the Track was skipped.
requirements.rationale: The example explicitly authorizes a relay processing a new upstream publication. It limits the lifetime of the prior PUBLISH_SKIPPED prohibition without requiring an original publisher to relay.

requirements.summary: After SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS cancellation, do not send further PUBLISH without knowing the client remains interested and authorized.
requirements.rationale: The same paragraph explicitly says cancellation does not prohibit original publishers from further PUBLISH messages. The knowledge prerequisite is relay-specific.

requirements.summary: Send PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to any subscriber to indicate Tracks available in that namespace.
requirements.rationale: After SETUP, drive namespace publication and observe PUBLISH_NAMESPACE without requiring prior SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE. This grants an optional publisher advertisement, not permission to bypass other authorization rules.

requirements.summary: Send SUBSCRIBE or FETCH for Tracks in a namespace without first receiving its PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: This permission concerns a subscriber initiating Track requests using out-of-band knowledge. It is not a publisher requirement to advertise before accepting those requests.

requirements.summary: Send NAMESPACE for a namespace containing one or more originally published Tracks to every subscriber whose SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE prefix matches it.
requirements.rationale: Use known published namespaces and matching/nonmatching tuple prefixes, including an empty prefix. Verify NAMESPACE notifications on matching discovery response streams under Section 4.1 and exact-field prefix matching in Section 7.5; this is NAMESPACE, not PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, and does not require the original publisher to have received an upstream advertisement.

requirements.summary: Send NAMESPACE to every matching namespace subscriber after receiving an authorized upstream PUBLISH_NAMESPACE for that namespace.
requirements.rationale: This branch has a relay-only upstream authorization precondition. The original-publisher branch at the same lexical anchor is independently applicable and testable.

requirements.summary: Include AUTHORIZATION TOKEN in a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE whose namespace also falls under an active SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE prefix.
requirements.rationale: Establish prefix discovery then drive an authorized namespace advertisement under that prefix and inspect its AUTHORIZATION TOKEN parameter. A concurrent PUBLISH_NAMESPACE is valid and has an independent request-stream lifetime; unlike NAMESPACE notifications it can carry its own authorization.

requirements.summary: Report reception of a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE REQUEST_OK to the Application to guide namespace publication decisions.
requirements.rationale: The contribution publisher receives the success response, but its Application notification is internal and no further wire action is mandated. The draft says the information can guide searches for additional subscribers or abandonment of publication.

requirements.summary: Report reception of a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE REQUEST_ERROR to the Application to guide namespace publication decisions.
requirements.rationale: Reporting a rejection can fail independently of reporting a success. The notification and resulting Application policy are not established by the response or by any required follow-up message.

requirements.summary: Send exactly one REQUEST_OK or REQUEST_ERROR as the first response on a PUBLISH_NAMESPACE bidirectional stream.
requirements.rationale: The namespace advertisement receiver acts as subscriber. The publisher's reaction to duplicate responses is the following separate recommendation.

requirements.summary: Close the session with a protocol error if more than one response is received for PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: After a publisher opens PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, send duplicate REQUEST_OK or conflicting REQUEST_OK and REQUEST_ERROR on that stream and observe PROTOCOL_VIOLATION session closure. This targets the publisher response receiver and does not rename REQUEST_OK as a separate wire message.

requirements.summary: Avoid using PUBLISH_NAMESPACE to find paths through richly connected networks of relays.
requirements.rationale: This is relay-network routing guidance motivated by absence of loop protection, not a ban on an original publisher advertising a namespace to a relay. The contribution harness does not construct or evaluate routing paths.

requirements.summary: Send a SUBSCRIBE or FETCH for a Track to any publisher.
requirements.rationale: The permission selects a request destination in the subscriber role; it does not require a contribution publisher to subscribe or fetch.

requirements.summary: When an accepted PUBLISH_NAMESPACE exactly matches a Track's namespace, request that Track only from senders of such advertisements.
requirements.rationale: The antecedent is the subscriber selecting publishers; the condition requires exact namespace equality, not merely an overlapping namespace prefix.

requirements.summary: Aggregate filters on subscriptions, especially namespace subscriptions, to conserve resources.
requirements.rationale: Aggregation combines downstream subscriber demands in a relay. An original contribution publisher has no upstream aggregation role.

requirements.summary: Propagate subscription filters upstream, especially for namespace subscriptions, to protect resources from excessive load.
requirements.rationale: Forwarding aggregated filtering needs toward upstream publishers is a relay duty independent of locally aggregating them.

requirements.summary: Limit publishers in a namespace by rejecting or closing namespace subscriptions with NAMESPACE_TOO_LARGE.
requirements.rationale: This permission is in Relay Resource Protection in Large Namespaces and addresses relay publisher-count limits, not a universal original-publisher error policy.

requirements.summary: Reject or close namespace subscriptions with CONFLICTING_FILTERS when too many disjoint downstream filters are requested across subscribers.
requirements.rationale: The optional rejection addresses the relay's aggregation burden from many downstream subscribers; it does not override per-request INVALID_FILTER validation.

requirements.summary: Reject or close namespace subscriptions with PREFIX_OVERLAP when different subscribers force an aggregated upstream subscription to overlap.
requirements.rationale: This is the relay's optional response to upstream aggregation constraints caused by different downstream subscribers, not a prohibition on original publishers accepting overlapping requests.

requirements.summary: Make a best effort to apply a changed Subscriber Priority to all Objects that have not yet been scheduled; handling already scheduled Objects is implementation-dependent.
requirements.rationale: The publisher owns scheduling, but the relay-side boundary cannot establish which Objects were already scheduled or how best effort was applied. Section 5.1.2 explicitly leaves the scheduling point implementation-dependent; arrival order cannot prove this internal update.

requirements.summary: Among multiple schedulable Objects with different Subscriber Priorities, schedule the Object with the highest Subscriber Priority first; lower numeric values have higher priority.
requirements.rationale: Rule 1 governs a publisher's internal selection among simultaneously schedulable Objects, excluding Objects blocked by flow control. Lines 1760-1765 allow scheduling to mean either serialization or packet transmission, so peer arrival order is not a conformance oracle.

requirements.summary: For schedulable Objects with equal Subscriber Priority and different Publisher Priorities, schedule the Object with the highest Publisher Priority first.
requirements.rationale: Rule 2 is independently conditional on tied Subscriber Priority. Publisher Priority can override the Track default per Subgroup or Datagram, but the implementation-dependent scheduling point and transport reordering prevent an external wire-order assertion.

requirements.summary: For schedulable Objects in the same subscription and Track, with equal Subscriber and Publisher Priorities but different Groups, use the subscription's Group Order to select which is scheduled first, subject to the differing-fill-order exception.
requirements.rationale: Rule 3 applies only within one subscription and Track; it is not a general ordering guarantee across subscriptions or FETCH responses. Section 5.1.2 defines the scheduling point as implementation-dependent. The fill exception is classified separately.

requirements.summary: In rule 3's equal-priority, different-Group comparison, when the subscription fill's Group Order differs from the subscription's Group Order, schedule the subscription-delivered Object first.
requirements.rationale: This draft-21 fill exception is a separate scheduling branch. Section 9.20.9 confirms that FILL_PARAMETERS Group Order governs ordering relative to subscription-delivered Objects, but the scheduling stage remains internal and does not promise peer arrival order.

requirements.summary: For equal-priority schedulable Objects in the same Group, Track and subscription, schedule a fill-delivered Object before a subscription-delivered Object.
requirements.rationale: Rule 4 prefers fill within one Group, whereas rule 3's different-Group, differing-order exception prefers subscription delivery. This distinction is normative scheduler advice, but neither local eligibility nor the implementation-dependent scheduling point can be determined from peer delivery order.

requirements.summary: When rule 4's fill-versus-subscription tie-break does not decide the comparison, schedule the lower Subgroup ID first for equal-priority Subgroup Objects in the same subscription, Track and Group.
requirements.rationale: This branch compares Subgroup forwarding preferences after the earlier priority and fill rules. A receiver sees transmitted data rather than the publisher's set of schedulable Objects or scheduling decisions.

requirements.summary: When rule 4's fill-versus-subscription tie-break does not decide the comparison, schedule the lower Object ID first for equal-priority Datagram Objects in the same subscription, Track and Group.
requirements.rationale: The Datagram branch compares Object IDs rather than Subgroup IDs. Its scheduler recommendation cannot be evaluated from potentially reordered or lost datagrams at the receiving peer.

requirements.summary: In rule 4's remaining equal-priority, same-subscription, same-Track and same-Group tie, if the two Objects have different Forwarding Preferences, select the datagram first.
requirements.rationale: This final rule-4 branch distinguishes datagrams from Subgroup streams; it does not override earlier priority or fill tie-breaks. Local scheduling and transport delivery remain different observations under lines 1760-1765.

requirements.summary: Prioritize the control streams highest, ahead of bidirectional request streams and all Objects.
requirements.rationale: An endpoint acting as publisher shares this scheduling recommendation. Relative internal scheduling priority is not a guaranteed arrival order and has no specified external completion deadline.

requirements.summary: Prioritize bidirectional request streams ahead of all Objects, after the control streams.
requirements.rationale: The request-versus-Object relation is independently meaningful from highest control priority. The recommendation constrains a local scheduler whose underlying transport interface and timing are not exposed to this harness.

requirements.summary: Optionally prioritize bidirectional request streams relative to each other using Subscriber Priority when specified.
requirements.rationale: This permits a publisher endpoint's internal request-stream policy. Wire arrival order cannot establish which scheduler selected the order; absence of this optional policy is not a conformance failure.

requirements.summary: Respect subscribers' priorities for downstream subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: The sentence explicitly assigns this downstream forwarding policy to relays. The contribution publisher is not being evaluated as a forwarding relay.

requirements.summary: Respect original publishers' priorities for downstream subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: This is the relay's independent duty to respect the original publisher's priority. Mention of the original publisher does not make it the actor of the requirement.

requirements.summary: Avoid directly copying Subscriber Priority from incoming subscriptions into upstream subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: The relay can derive upstream policy from popularity, local policy or a common value. The contribution publisher does not perform upstream subscription aggregation for downstream subscribers.

requirements.summary: Avoid directly copying Group Order from incoming subscriptions into upstream subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: This separately names the upstream Group Order choice as relay policy. It is outside contribution-publisher behavior even though relays also act as publishers on downstream sessions.

requirements.summary: If a default priority exists, set it near the middle of the range, for example 128, so non-default priorities can be higher or lower.
requirements.rationale: A publisher implementation is included, but this advice neither fixes a unique midpoint nor identifies a wire field that proves the implementation's default policy. Sections 9.20.8 and 10.4 separately specify defaults for particular fields; those definitions do not turn this general recommendation into an exact-value test.

requirements.summary: When OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT is nonzero, retain when the last header byte of each Object was received upstream or provided by the original publisher application.
requirements.rationale: Original-publisher timestamp retention is an internal state requirement. Observable expiration actions are classified separately; no wire event proves that a particular timestamp was retained rather than an equivalent internal mechanism used.

requirements.summary: For a Subgroup Object subject to a nonzero OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT, check elapsed time before attempting to pass the Object to the underlying transport for transmission.
requirements.rationale: The exact pre-transport check point is local to the publisher. Packet arrival does not identify when bytes entered the transport; the next clause supplies the externally observable reset outcome.

requirements.summary: If a Subgroup Object's elapsed time exceeds its effective nonzero OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT before handoff to the transport, reset the underlying stream using DELIVERY_TIMEOUT.
requirements.rationale: The required reset depends on expiry before transport handoff, an internal condition unavailable to the approved external harness. Peer flow control cannot prove that condition because the transport may buffer bytes without sending them, and late arrival does not establish when admission occurred. Publisher instrumentation or internal adapter diagnostics do not count as external protocol evidence. Effective timeouts use the first Object's override or Track value and the smaller nonzero subscriber value. Section 11.3.2 supplies closure context; Section 12.5 defines DELIVERY_TIMEOUT as 0x2.

requirements.summary: After an Object delivery timeout resets a Subgroup stream, avoid opening a new stream to deliver additional Objects in that same Subgroup.
requirements.rationale: After observing the timeout reset, supply more Objects with the same Group and Subgroup IDs and inspect subsequent streams during the bounded fixture. This checks a concrete attempted reopening, not inferred scheduler state or a prohibition on other Subgroups.

requirements.summary: Check Object delivery timeouts before retransmitting Object data when the underlying transport implementation permits it.
requirements.rationale: Both availability of the transport hook and the pre-retransmission check are internal. A peer cannot distinguish permitted transport limitations from a missing check; the source gives no unconditional wire outcome for this recommendation.

requirements.summary: Minimize data buffered at the underlying transport layer because such buffered data can no longer be timed out and can be transmitted after expiry.
requirements.rationale: Transport queue occupancy and the meaning of minimize have no external numeric bound. The explicit warning about already-buffered expired data prevents treating every late received Object as a delivery-timeout violation.

requirements.summary: Drop Object datagrams when their elapsed time exceeds the effective nonzero OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT.
requirements.rationale: The approved external harness cannot determine whether a datagram expired before entering the underlying transport queue. Peer flow control does not expose admission, late arrival can result from permitted transport buffering, and non-arrival can result from packet loss rather than a timeout drop. Publisher instrumentation or internal adapter diagnostics do not count as external protocol evidence. For Datagram forwarding, SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT also acts as an Object timeout and the smaller nonzero value applies; data already queued in transport is excluded by this section's buffering caveat.

requirements.summary: Either minimize datagram queueing or use a datagram queue mechanism with time bounds, such as WebTransport outgoingMaxAge.
requirements.rationale: These are alternatives for meeting one queueing recommendation, not two mandatory policies. Internal queue size or choice of a time-bounded API cannot be established from delivered datagrams, and minimize has no numeric threshold.

requirements.summary: For Subgroup forwarding with nonzero SUBGROUP_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT, start a timer of that duration when all Subgroup Objects are known published, through upstream FIN or notification by the original publisher application.
requirements.rationale: The original publisher's notification and timer creation are local state. The timer does not begin merely because a subscriber saw the last Object. The next clause separately defines the reset observable under a controlled completion trigger.

requirements.summary: If the nonzero Subgroup delivery timer expires before the underlying stream reaches all data committed, reset that stream.
requirements.rationale: A driven application can announce Subgroup completion at a known time while the controlled receiver withholds acknowledgments, ensuring the stream cannot be fully committed; a reset then provides the bounded wire outcome. This clause does not specify a reset code, unlike the OBJECT_DELIVERY_TIMEOUT reset at line 1862. Section 11.3.2 permits a reset after a sent FIN and explains the closure context.

requirements.summary: If a subscriber consumes Objects too slowly and causes the publisher to exceed its resource limits, optionally terminate that subscription using PUBLISH_DONE with TOO_FAR_BEHIND.
requirements.rationale: Use a declared resource limit and a deliberately stalled subscriber to observe this optional termination capability. The draft supplies the message and error, not a universal resource threshold; continuing the subscription is not a required-conformance failure.

requirements.summary: Do not use a moqt URI whose authority has an empty host portion.
requirements.rationale: A contribution client uses a URI, but parsing a locally supplied malformed URI has no prescribed peer-visible error in this clause; failure to connect does not establish the reason. Native-QUIC AUTHORITY validation and its errors are specified separately in Section 9.1.1, not invented here.

requirements.summary: Optionally use fragment identifiers with moqt URIs; process the fragment locally after establishing the session and do not transmit it to the server.
requirements.rationale: This permission covers a client publisher, but its capability is local fragment processing. A fragment's absence from the wire does not prove that processing occurred. The required registered syntax is a separate anchor and Section 16.3's registry is initially empty.

requirements.actor: endpoint using a MOQT URI fragment
requirements.summary: Begin a moqt URI fragment with a registered fragment type identifier, followed by a colon and a type-specific value.
requirements.rationale: Fragments are processed locally and are not transmitted to the relay-side peer. Section 16.3 makes the fragment registry initially empty, so this draft supplies no registered type for a positive fixture. No local failure API or wire error is specified for malformed fragments.

requirements.actor: endpoint using a MOQT URI fragment
requirements.summary: Use only ASCII lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (a-z, 0-9, -) in fragment type identifiers.
requirements.rationale: This syntax constraint applies to URI-using contribution clients but the identifier is never transmitted. The grammar can be unit-tested in a client parser, not inferred from a connection at the runner's protocol boundary.

requirements.summary: When SVCB-compatible records are published for the authority, optionally use them to learn server endpoints and supported ALPN protocols before connecting.
requirements.rationale: A publisher client can use this discovery mechanism, but the chosen endpoint and ALPN do not reveal whether DNS records, cache or configuration supplied them. DNS resolver instrumentation is outside this relay-side protocol boundary. The text separately describes HTTPS records for WebTransport and retains a TODO for the moqt SVCB draft.

requirements.summary: Optionally establish a native QUIC MOQT session when the server selects a supported MOQT ALPN from the client's TLS ClientHello offer.
requirements.rationale: The runner can observe successful native QUIC negotiation and MOQT initialization for draft 21. Section 6.2 defines draft ALPNs using the draft number, and Section 6.2.2 specifies the native session path. This MAY permits a transport choice rather than requiring both transports.

requirements.summary: Optionally establish MOQT over WebTransport, using the h3 selection on QUIC or the h2 offer on TCP+TLS described here and the WebTransport establishment procedure in Section 6.2.1.
requirements.rationale: An HTTP/3 extended CONNECT and WT-Available-Protocols negotiation followed by MOQT setup provide observable optional capability. Section 6.1.2 also describes TCP+TLS/h2, while Section 6.2 says the protocol is not defined over other transports such as TCP; preserve this wording tension and do not infer a native TCP MOQT protocol or require an HTTP/2 runner. The draft does not impose a separate WebTransport reliability-mode prohibition in this range.

requirements.summary: Support the QUIC DATAGRAM extension on the QUIC connection used for MOQT.
requirements.rationale: The controlled peer can offer QUIC DATAGRAM and establish that the publisher advertises usable extension support. This is required for a MOQT QUIC connection even when a particular Track sends only streams, and the text notes that WebTransport over HTTP/3 already requires it.

requirements.summary: Negotiate the QUIC DATAGRAM extension in the QUIC connection used for MOQT.
requirements.rationale: Transport negotiation is visible independently of compiled-in support: a connection on which the extension was not negotiated must not proceed as a valid MOQT session. The clause covers native QUIC and WebTransport over HTTP/3; it names neither a MOQT error code for negotiation failure nor a reliability-mode value.

requirements.summary: Do not begin a bidirectional request stream with a message other than TRACK_STATUS, SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, FETCH, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE or SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS unless that other message type was negotiated.
requirements.rationale: Inspect each publisher-opened bidirectional stream's first message with the negotiated extension set. SETUP belongs on each peer's unidirectional control stream and Objects on unidirectional data streams; neither is silently added to the seven default request openers.

requirements.summary: Close the session with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION if a bidirectional stream begins with a message other than the seven permitted request types or a negotiated alternative.
requirements.rationale: The runner opens a bidirectional stream with an unnegotiated invalid initial message and observes the publisher endpoint's session close and specified error. This receiver duty is distinct from the sender's placement prohibition.

requirements.summary: Buffer Object data arriving on unidirectional streams before the control streams until both control streams arrive and setup is complete.
requirements.rationale: Receiving Objects is the subscriber side of this combined sentence. The contribution publisher sends Objects and is not evaluated as an Object-consuming subscriber.

requirements.summary: Buffer data arriving on bidirectional streams beginning with request messages before the control streams until both control streams arrive and setup is complete.
requirements.rationale: A publisher can receive early requests, but internal buffering is not established by a later successful response. The next paragraph explicitly permits resets when buffering is unwanted or the message type is unsupported, so there is no unconditional bounded response proving this storage policy.

requirements.summary: Before session and control-stream establishment, optionally reset an early bidirectional request stream if buffering is unwanted or its message type is unsupported.
requirements.rationale: Send an early request before delivering the peer SETUP and observe this permitted stream reset. The permission applies to bidirectional request streams, not an invented reset rule for every early unidirectional Object stream; buffering instead is also permitted.

requirements.summary: Do not close a control stream at the underlying transport layer during the session's lifetime; such closure results in session closure as PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
requirements.rationale: Track the publisher's unidirectional control stream for a FIN or reset while the MOQT session is active. The prohibition does not prevent session termination itself; the next sentence states the consequence of premature control closure.

requirements.summary: Avoid using Message Parameters requiring negotiation before receiving the peer SETUP, unless the application requires the extension or the endpoint knows the peer supports it.
requirements.rationale: A driven fresh-client fixture with no preconfigured peer support and no required application extension can inspect parameters sent before delivery of peer SETUP. Without those declared preconditions, early use cannot be scored as a violation. Section 9.20 distinguishes base-version parameters from negotiated extensions and explains the unknown-parameter termination consequence.

requirements.summary: Optionally defer upstream subscription initiation until handshake completion to mitigate resource exhaustion from replayed packets.
requirements.rationale: The permission concerns a relay opening upstream subscriptions on behalf of replayed requests, not the original contribution publisher's own publication.

requirements.summary: Optionally reject 0-RTT entirely to mitigate resource exhaustion from replayed packets.
requirements.rationale: Rejecting 0-RTT is the second independent relay mitigation. Section 6.3.1 does not require a contribution client to implement or accept 0-RTT.

requirements.summary: Include in SETUP all Setup Options required by Section 9.1 for the negotiated MOQT version.
requirements.rationale: Decode the publisher's SETUP against the negotiated draft and transport. Sections 9.1.1 and 9.1.2 require AUTHORITY and PATH for a native client using a moqt URI but prohibit them for servers and WebTransport; optional/defaulted options are not promoted to universally required fields. SETUP exchange determines extensions after both messages have been sent and received.

requirements.summary: In a new MOQT version, specify which existing extensions can be used with that version.
requirements.rationale: This is a normative specification-author obligation, not an endpoint implementation action or quoted informative vocabulary.

requirements.summary: In a new extension, specify the existing MOQT versions with which the extension can be used.
requirements.rationale: Compatibility declarations belong to authors of extension specifications. A contribution publisher cannot satisfy or violate this document-authoring requirement through a wire interaction.

requirements.summary: Close the session upon receiving an unknown unidirectional stream type.
requirements.rationale: Inject a stream type outside Table 2 and all negotiated extensions, then observe session termination. This clause does not name an error code; do not borrow PROTOCOL_VIOLATION from the distinct bidirectional first-message rule or from another draft.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_REQUEST_ID when a received Request ID has the wrong least significant bit for its sender: clients use even IDs and servers use odd IDs.
requirements.rationale: The runner sends an otherwise valid request with parity inconsistent with its client/server role and observes the specific session error. Sender role, not publisher/subscriber role, determines parity.

requirements.summary: Close the session with INVALID_REQUEST_ID when a duplicate Request ID is received.
requirements.rationale: Request IDs are session-wide across SUBSCRIBE, PUBLISH, FETCH, SUBSCRIBE_NAMESPACE, SUBSCRIBE_TRACKS, PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, REQUEST_UPDATE and TRACK_STATUS. Reuse a prior ID with valid parity to isolate duplicate rejection; response messages carry no Request ID in this draft.

requirements.summary: Do not send FIN on a request-stream direction until all messages required for that request type on that direction have been sent.
requirements.rationale: A bidirectional stream is ordered separately in each direction, so the peer can decode every message before FIN and compare with that request type's requirements. FIN means no further messages, not request cancellation; an abrupt reset is a different operation.

requirements.summary: Send the corresponding response message before sending FIN on the response direction of a request stream.
requirements.rationale: The publisher responds to relay requests. Stream ordering provides direct evidence of a response preceding FIN, independently of the more general all-required-messages rule and the Established-subscription PUBLISH_DONE rule.

requirements.summary: For an Established subscription, send PUBLISH_DONE before sending FIN on the request-stream direction.
requirements.rationale: The publisher obligation holds for Established subscriptions initiated through either PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE. Inspect the same request-stream direction for PUBLISH_DONE before graceful FIN; the clause does not require PUBLISH_DONE for a never-established rejected request or turn a reset into a FIN.

requirements.summary: After the responder sends its response, any subsequent required messages and FIN to signal completion, send FIN on the requester's direction if it has not already done so.
requirements.rationale: For a completed publisher-originated request, the runner supplies the valid terminal responder messages and FIN, then observes reciprocal graceful closure in a bounded run. The draft gives no numeric latency bound; an observation deadline records inconclusive non-completion rather than inventing an exact timing requirement.

requirements.summary: Send FIN promptly after a message when nothing further will be sent on that direction and no response to a future REQUEST_UPDATE will be needed.
requirements.rationale: The peer cannot establish the endpoint's future-message intentions, and promptly has no specified deadline. The concrete response-before-FIN and PUBLISH_DONE-before-FIN wire rules remain independently testable.

requirements.summary: A requester, except a sender of PUBLISH, may send FIN immediately after a message if it will not send REQUEST_UPDATE.
requirements.rationale: A contribution publisher can originate PUBLISH_NAMESPACE, so the permission is applicable even though PUBLISH itself is excluded. With an update-free driven request, observe FIN immediately after the request on that direction; the stream remains open in the responder's direction and the FIN does not cancel the request.

requirements.summary: Optionally cancel an opened request, as either requester or responder, using RESET_STREAM for its sending direction when that direction is still open.
requirements.rationale: Cancellation is optional, but its transport mechanism is explicit. A driven publisher withdrawal or rejection can expose RESET_STREAM on the still-open send direction; the separate receive direction requires its own action and FIN is not a cancellation substitute.

requirements.summary: Optionally cancel an opened request using STOP_SENDING for its receiving direction when that direction is still open, including when the endpoint has already sent FIN on its sending direction.
requirements.rationale: A requester or responder can cancel; STOP_SENDING independently terminates the receive direction. A prior local FIN cannot cancel the still-open remote direction, so include a cancellation-after-FIN scenario rather than treating half-closure as full cancellation.

requirements.summary: When rejecting a request without any application processing, send REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: Under a declared pre-application rejection condition, such as a configured unsupported request, observe the publisher's error response. The scenario must establish that condition independently; the wire response alone cannot prove whether application processing occurred. The clause does not prescribe one universal error code.

requirements.summary: When rejecting a request without any application processing, gracefully close its sending direction with FIN after REQUEST_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: The error response and FIN are independently observable requirements under the same declared rejection precondition. Section 6.4.2.2 requires the response before FIN; bidirectional directions close independently, so this does not require an endpoint to send FIN for its peer.

requirements.summary: Do not publish application Tracks whose Track Namespace first field is .session.
requirements.rationale: A driven application fixture identifies its attempted Track publication so the runner can detect forbidden PUBLISH or resulting Track delivery. Session-level Tracks managed by the MOQT implementation for an extension are distinct and must not be rejected merely because their first field is .session.

requirements.summary: Do not publish application namespaces whose first field is .session.
requirements.rationale: Namespace publication is independently observable from Track publication when the driven application tries to advertise a known namespace. The restriction targets the first namespace field and the application actor, preserving MOQT-managed extension namespaces.

requirements.summary: Do not forward requests for session-level Tracks to other sessions.
requirements.rationale: This is a cross-session forwarding prohibition on relays. The contribution-publisher harness does not serve downstream subscribers or test relay forwarding.

requirements.summary: Do not forward requests for session-level namespaces to other sessions.
requirements.rationale: Namespace request forwarding is independently prohibited but remains relay-only. It is not a ban on a publisher processing session-level requests locally.

requirements.summary: Reject with DOES_NOT_EXIST a request whose Track Namespace first field is .session and whose Track Name is empty.
requirements.rationale: Send a Track request with the reserved first field and an empty Track Name, including a multi-field namespace case, and observe the defined rejection. The normative sentence tests the first field, rather than only an exact one-field .session tuple.

requirements.summary: Reject a request for an unrecognized session-level Track with REQUEST_ERROR using DOES_NOT_EXIST.
requirements.rationale: Use a nonempty Track Name under .session that is unrecognized by the declared extension set and inspect the publisher endpoint's error. Section 16.10 defines registration of session-level names; no arbitrary extension Track is assumed supported. Application dispatch is classified separately.

requirements.summary: Reject a request for an unrecognized session-level namespace with REQUEST_ERROR using DOES_NOT_EXIST.
requirements.rationale: A namespace request has a different target from a Track request; submit an unrecognized namespace beneath the reserved first field and observe the specified request error. The condition is unrecognized session-level names, not every unknown application namespace.

requirements.summary: Handle an unrecognized session-level Track request by rejecting it within MOQT rather than passing it to the Application.
requirements.rationale: The same normative clause also constrains internal dispatch: a wire REQUEST_ERROR cannot prove that no Application callback ran. Keep the local handling duty separate from the externally testable rejection instead of claiming the error establishes both.

requirements.summary: Handle an unrecognized session-level namespace request by rejecting it within MOQT rather than passing it to the Application.
requirements.rationale: Namespace dispatch can differ from Track dispatch. This application-boundary prohibition is applicable to a publisher endpoint, but the runner cannot observe callbacks and does not equate a correct error response with proof of internal routing.

requirements.summary: Optionally treat a subscription- or request-specific error as a session error and close the entire session in selected circumstances, considering the impact on other outstanding subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: The publisher endpoint can choose this policy, but the circumstances and consideration of other subscriptions are unspecified internal decisions. A generic close does not establish why it happened and no deterministic error stimulus must select escalation under this permission.

requirements.summary: After the timeout indicated by a session-level GOAWAY, close the session with GOAWAY_TIMEOUT if subscriptions or fetches remain open.
requirements.rationale: Section 9.2 allows either endpoint to send control-stream GOAWAY, so a client publisher is included. Use a declared nonzero timeout and keep a subscription open to observe GOAWAY_TIMEOUT. Section 9.2 treats zero as no specific timeout and permits early closure; no evaluator may demand that the sender wait at least the hint. This paragraph names subscriptions or fetches, Section 9.2 says open requests, and line 2428 says a peer that has not closed; preserve those differing conditions rather than broadening this anchor.

requirements.actor: server acting as subscriber and relay
requirements.summary: When the server is a subscriber, send GOAWAY to downstream subscribers before unsubscribing from upstream publishers.
requirements.rationale: The stated topology has downstream subscribers and upstream publishers, so this is a relay/server-subscriber migration ordering rule. It does not require an original contribution publisher to invent downstream subscriber sessions.

requirements.summary: After receiving GOAWAY, wait until no Established subscriptions remain before closing the session with NO_ERROR.
requirements.rationale: RECOMMENDED normalizes to Should. A client contribution publisher owns Established subscriptions as their publisher; send a control-stream GOAWAY and track subscription completion relative to its NO_ERROR close. The surrounding text allows delayed closure for more Objects and describes migration of subscriptions and published namespaces as ideal, not separate mandatory actions under this keyword. A sender's GOAWAY_TIMEOUT closure is a distinct outcome.

requirements.summary: Optionally cache Objects; a relay is not required to provide a cache.
requirements.rationale: This grants an intermediary a caching capability. An original contribution publisher's retention of its own Objects is not the relay cache described here.

requirements.summary: Ignore subsequently received Objects with the same Full Track Name, Group ID and Object ID as a cached Object.
requirements.rationale: Deduplicating received Objects in an intermediary cache does not apply to the original publisher role. The alternative update permission is classified separately at occurrence 2.

requirements.summary: Use a duplicate Object to update its cached existence state from existing to not existing when the Object is no longer available.
requirements.rationale: This is the first permitted cache-field update, constrained to the one-way state transition in Section 2.1.1. Cache poisoning protection concerns the relay, not the contribution publisher.

requirements.summary: Use a duplicate Object to add, remove or update cached Object Properties, subject to the constraints of each property.
requirements.rationale: The second permitted category of cache update is independent of the existence-state update. It does not permit changes to immutable Object fields or impose relay cache behavior on a publisher.

requirements.summary: Treat a Track as Malformed after receiving a duplicate Object with a different Forwarding Preference, Subgroup ID, Priority or Payload.
requirements.rationale: Although the actor is an endpoint rather than only a relay, receiving track Objects is a subscriber role. An original contribution publisher sends Objects; its own field-stability duties are separate requirements and do not make this receiver reaction applicable.

requirements.summary: Change the representation of a range of nonexistent Objects to a semantically equivalent representation.
requirements.rationale: This relay permission includes equivalent End-of-Group signaling and removing a redundant Prior Group ID Gap in FETCH. It is not permission for the publisher to change which Objects exist.

requirements.summary: Do not cache a received Object after recording that the Object does not exist.
requirements.rationale: This concerns relay cache admission. Section 2.1 explicitly allows late receipt after a nonexistence indication without making the Track malformed; it does not create a publisher error rule.

requirements.summary: Do not forward a received Object after recording that the Object does not exist.
requirements.rationale: Forwarding is independently observable from caching but belongs to the same caching-relay actor. The runner does not forward to downstream subscribers or score publisher behavior as relay forwarding.

requirements.summary: Store every Object field defined in Section 11.1.1, except Object Properties whose definitions specify otherwise.
requirements.rationale: In this Caching Relays section, the cache retains received Object identity, priority, forwarding, subgroup, status, property and payload fields. The publisher's original content store is not this relay cache.

requirements.summary: Set Forward=1 upstream when at least one downstream subscriber to the Track has Forward=1.
requirements.rationale: This aggregates downstream demand into an upstream relay subscription. When all downstream Forward values are zero, the relay has discretion; neither case creates an upstream-subscription duty for an original publisher.

requirements.summary: Handle Objects for the same Track received from multiple publishers.
requirements.rationale: The relay merges multiple publication sources. The preceding paragraph allows rejection of additional publishers due to implementation constraints; this is not an unlimited-capacity requirement and not an original-publisher duty.

requirements.summary: Forward Objects received from multiple publishers of the same Track to matching Established subscriptions.
requirements.rationale: Downstream forwarding is separate from accepting multiple upstream sources. Both operations require a relay topology outside original contribution publishing.

requirements.summary: Attempt to deduplicate Objects before forwarding, subject to implementation constraints.
requirements.rationale: The advice addresses relay forwarding of Objects from multiple publishers. It does not impose perfect deduplication or apply to an original publisher.

requirements.summary: Ensure subscribers are authorized to access the content associated with the requested Track.
requirements.rationale: The named actor is the relay handling SUBSCRIBE or FETCH. Authorization may be supplied by the request or session and its mechanism is out of scope; the sentence does not impose a relay authorization service on the publisher.

requirements.summary: Have an Established upstream subscription before sending SUBSCRIBE_OK for a downstream SUBSCRIBE.
requirements.rationale: The upstream-before-downstream dependency is specific to relays. An original publisher owns the Track rather than subscribing to an upstream source.

requirements.summary: Withhold FETCH_OK until sufficient information is available to send it when that information is not available immediately upon FETCH receipt.
requirements.rationale: This is a relay information-availability guard; the actor is not every FETCH responder. Original-publisher FETCH response requirements are inventoried in their own sections.

requirements.summary: Follow Section 9.20.18 LARGEST_OBJECT constraints, including selecting the maximum upstream advertised or received Object Location.
requirements.rationale: The referenced section combines LARGEST_OBJECT received in upstream SUBSCRIBE_OK, PUBLISH or REQUEST_UPDATE_OK with received Object Locations. That relay aggregation rule remains separate from the original publisher's own LARGEST_OBJECT duties.

requirements.summary: Do not reorder Objects received on a multi-object stream when forwarding them to subscribers.
requirements.rationale: Preservation of received stream order is an intermediary duty. It is not a general cross-stream ordering rule or an original-publisher scheduling rule.

requirements.summary: Do not drop Objects received on a multi-object stream when forwarding them to subscribers.
requirements.rationale: Dropping and reordering are distinct forbidden forwarding actions. The preceding paragraph describes subscription filters and delivery constraints; this row preserves the multi-object-stream context without converting it into a publisher-wide loss prohibition.

requirements.summary: Aggregate authorized subscriptions for a Track requested by multiple subscribers into a shared upstream subscription.
requirements.rationale: Sharing upstream content among multiple downstream requests is an optional relay capability. The original publisher does not own this aggregation topology.

requirements.summary: Combine downstream subscriber filters on an upstream subscription, up to the peer's MAX_FILTER_RANGES.
requirements.rationale: The range-count limit constrains relay aggregation; the following discussion permits removing filters or opening more upstream subscriptions if addition is impossible. None of this is an original-publisher duty.

requirements.summary: Optionally migrate Established subscriptions to a new relay after GOAWAY or a network switch without QUIC Connection Migration, cancelling old subscriptions after successful new ones.
requirements.rationale: This is explicitly subscriber-side relay switchover. Publisher-side migration has a separate permission in Section 7.5.1.

requirements.summary: Pause a PUBLISH-initiated subscription using REQUEST_UPDATE with Forward State=0 until subscribers for the new Track are known.
requirements.rationale: The relay chooses whether to pause pending downstream interest. Publisher handling of a received Forward update is independently applicable elsewhere, but does not change the actor of this permission.

requirements.summary: Verify that a publisher is authorized to publish the Tracks whose namespace matches its PUBLISH_NAMESPACE.
requirements.rationale: This authorization check belongs to the relay receiving the namespace publication. The checked set of Tracks differs from the individual-track check in the next clause.

requirements.summary: Verify that a publisher is authorized to publish the Full Track Name in a PUBLISH message.
requirements.rationale: The relay verifies an individual Track publication. The contribution publisher is the subject of that authorization decision, not the actor required to perform this relay check.

requirements.summary: Do not assume authorization to publish a single Track implicitly authorizes the publisher to publish other Tracks.
requirements.rationale: This relay authorization boundary has a line-split MUST NOT and a sentence continuing across the page break. It does not prescribe the original publisher's authorization policy.

requirements.summary: Do not assume authorization to publish a single Track implicitly authorizes the publisher to publish Track Namespaces.
requirements.rationale: Namespace publication authorization is distinct from permission to publish additional individual Tracks. Both prohibitions address relay policy enforcement.
